draft.title: Epidemiology
card: Epidemiology is the study of patterns of disease in populations. Epidemiologists compare groups to find possible causes and to test whether a treatment works.
Incidence
the number of new cases of a disease in a population during a set time, such as one year.
Prevalence
the number of people who have a disease in a population at a given time, counting both new and existing cases.
Mortality
the number of deaths from a disease in a population over a set time.
draft.remember: Incidence counts new cases, prevalence counts all current cases, mortality counts deaths.

a.q: In one year, 300 people in a town are newly diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. Which measure does this number describe?
opts: Incidence
Prevalence
Mortality
Risk factor
a.why: Incidence counts new cases in a set time, and these 300 are new diagnoses in one year. Prevalence is the tempting choice, but it would also count people who already had diabetes before that year.
a.clue: Are these cases new, or all cases present?

b.q: A region's asthma prevalence rises for ten years, but its incidence stays the same each year. Which explanation fits best?
opts: People are living longer with the condition
More people are newly getting asthma each year
The mortality rate has fallen to zero
The condition is spreading from person to person
b.why: Prevalence counts all current cases. If new cases stay steady but people live longer with the condition, the total number of people with it grows. A rise in new cases would instead raise incidence.
b.clue: Prevalence counts new and existing cases together.

b.best: People are living longer with the condition

problems.detail: The distractor 'The mortality rate has fallen to zero' also predicts a rise in prevalence with steady incidence, because fewer people leave the pool of cases. 'Zero' makes it implausible, but a careful student could see it as consistent. Consider a distractor that clearly does not raise prevalence, such as 'People are recovering from asthma faster'.

proposal.title: Epidemiology
card: Epidemiology is the study of patterns of disease in populations. Epidemiologists compare groups to find possible causes and to test whether a treatment works.
Incidence
the number of new cases of a disease in a population during a set time, such as one year.
Prevalence
the number of people who have a disease in a population at a given time, counting both new and existing cases. It grows when new cases outnumber the people leaving through recovery or death.
Mortality
the number of deaths from a disease in a population over a set time.
proposal.remember: Incidence counts new cases, prevalence counts all current cases, mortality counts deaths.

a.q: In one year, 300 people in a town are newly diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. Which measure does this number describe?

b.q: A region's asthma prevalence rises for ten years, but its incidence stays the same each year. Which explanation fits best?

b.why: Prevalence counts all current cases. If new cases stay steady but people live longer with the condition, fewer leave the total, so it grows. Faster recovery would do the opposite, as people would leave the total sooner and prevalence would fall.
